user:
Handbook: Official MTO Driver's Handbook (Ontario, Canada)
Units: metric (m, km, km/h)
Topic: passing
Batch: 14 passages from the page "Sharing the road": m76, m54, m55, m59, m56, m57, m58, m60, m96, m65, m66, m69, m70, m71.

[m76] page: Sharing the road | heading: Pedestrians · item 2 | text
Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk. A stopped vehicle may be a clue that a pedestrian is crossing.

[m54] page: Sharing the road | heading: Cyclists · ¶1 | text
However, they can use any part of the lane if necessary for safety, such as to:

[m55] page: Sharing the road | heading: Cyclists · item 3 | text
Discourage passing where the lane is too narrow to be shared safely

[m59] page: Sharing the road | heading: Cyclists · Diagram 2-11 | figure
Figure: Diagram 2-11 | Alt text: “bike lane adjacent to parking bays”

[m56] page: Sharing the road | heading: Cyclists · ¶3 | text
When passing a cyclist, drivers of motor vehicles must maintain a minimum distance of one metre, where practical between their vehicle and the cyclist.

[m57] page: Sharing the road | heading: Cyclists · ¶3 | text
(See Diagram 2-11.) Failure to do so may result in a fine and an additional two demerit points on the driver’s record.

[m58] page: Sharing the road | heading: Cyclists · ¶3 | text
Whenever possible, you should change lanes to pass.

[m60] page: Sharing the road | heading: Cyclists · ¶6 | text
Do not sound your horn unnecessarily when you are overtaking a cyclist. It may frighten them and cause them to lose control. If you feel that you must use your horn, tap it quickly and lightly while you are still some distance away from the cyclist.

[m96] page: Sharing the road | heading: Cyclists · ¶12 | text
When parked on the side of the roadway, look behind you and check your mirrors and blind spots for a passing cyclist before opening a door.

[m65] page: Sharing the road | heading: Large commercial vehicles · ¶3 | text
When passing a large vehicle, do not cut in front closely. Not only is this discourteous, it is dangerous; it reduces the space cushion large vehicles require in order to stop safely. Allow more room when passing a large vehicle.

[m66] page: Sharing the road | heading: Large commercial vehicles · ¶8 | text
6. Turbulence - Due to various factors such as air pressure and airflow, a large vehicle can create heavy air turbulence. This may affect your ability to control your vehicle when passing a large one.

[m69] page: Sharing the road | heading: Farm machinery · ¶2 | text
Stay well back and do not pass until it is safe to do so.

[m70] page: Sharing the road | heading: Horse-drawn vehicles · ¶2 | text
Maintain a safe following distance and only pass when it is safe to do so.

[m71] page: Sharing the road | heading: Horse-drawn vehicles · ¶2 | text
When passing, give as much distance between you and them as possible. Passing too closely could scare or startle the horse, causing it to change direction suddenly on the roadway.

Write the reading notes for all 14 passages, then the statements, following sections 4 and 5. Return only the JSON object.

figure: diagram of bike lane adjacent to parking bays; no specific passing rule stated in alt text
rule: drivers must maintain a minimum distance of 1 m when passing a cyclist, where practical
penalty: failure to maintain 1 m distance when passing a cyclist may result in a fine and 2 demerit points
rule: drivers should change lanes to pass a cyclist whenever possible
rule: do not sound horn unnecessarily when overtaking a cyclist; rule: if horn is used, tap it quickly and lightly from a distance
rule: check for passing cyclists before opening a door when parked
rule: do not cut in front closely when passing a large vehicle; rule: allow more room when passing a large vehicle
fact: large vehicles create air turbulence that may affect vehicle control when passing
rule: stay well back from farm machinery and do not pass until safe to do so
rule: maintain safe following distance from horse-drawn vehicles and only pass when safe to do so

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT pass a vehicle WHEN the vehicle is stopped at a crosswalk BECAUSE a stopped vehicle may be a clue that a pedestrian is crossing

statements.text: FACT a cyclist can use any part of the lane if necessary for safety, such as to discourage passing where the lane is too narrow to be shared safely

sources.quote: However, they can use any part of the lane if necessary for safety, such as to:
Discourage passing where the lane is too narrow to be shared safely

statements.note: Combined m54 and m55 to capture the full condition and purpose.

statements.text: a driver MUST maintain a minimum distance of 1 m between the vehicle and the cyclist WHEN passing a cyclist WHERE PRACTICAL IF VIOLATED a fine AND 2 demerit points

Failure to do so may result in a fine and an additional two demerit points on the driver’s record.

flags.note: The condition 'where practical' is subjective and not defined by a specific measure.
